_comment: SHOSMED physics, FINAL block. Implemented 20 November 2026 from
SHOSMED_Physics_Final_Block_Review_and_Claude_Prompt.txt.
HOW THE IDS WERE VERIFIED. The review supplied 41 displays, not 40, and
warned against inferring a phys-241..phys-280 mapping from the apparent
order. Each display was matched by FULL CONTENT MATCH of its ORIGINAL stem
plus all four ORIGINAL option texts against all 280 physics records, on a
canonical form that decodes named HTML entities, strips tags, folds
sub/superscripts to plain digits and normalises dashes, Greek letters,
arrows and whitespace.
- All 41 matched EXACTLY. No match was ambiguous and none needed the
explanation as a tie-break.
- Q1 resolved to phys-214, which is the record approved as batch 4 Q34,
exactly as the review states. It is kept byte-identical and adds no new
coverage.
- Q2..Q41 resolved to phys-241..phys-280, which is EXACTLY the set of 40
physics records left unreviewed after the four earlier blocks. That
equality was computed, not assumed from the numbering.
- Every stored topic equalled the signature topic, and all 41 stored
answer letters equalled the review key block. No key was changed and no
stored key conflicts with the scientific key.
THREE BANDS, confirmed in storage rather than assumed:
- Q1 (phys-214): the batch 4 structure, frozen.
- Q2..Q11 (phys-241..phys-250): an educational-point block and a Bottom
Line, no Key Concept, and three lettered feedback paragraphs already
stored, 33 bodies in all. Q9 has four points; the other nine blocks have
three each, 31 points in 10 blocks.
- Q12..Q41 (phys-251..phys-280): one Key Concept each and NO feedback of
any kind. The 90 supplied bodies were therefore added, three per item,
between the main explanation and the Key Concept. Nothing was
duplicated: the export’s claim that these expose no bodies matches
storage exactly.
- The finished block carries 123 distractor bodies, 31 Key Concepts (Q1
and Q12..Q41), 31 educational points in 10 blocks and 10 Bottom Lines.
HEADINGS. All 41 keyed headings already reproduced their keyed option, so
none needed re-synchronizing except where an option text itself changed
(Q4 B, Q5 B, Q11 C, Q37 C). Three stored feedback headings in the second
band abbreviated their option (Q6 D, Q8 A, Q8 D) and were synchronized, as
the review directs. Q1 is exempt from all heading work.
NOTATION, inspected rather than assumed. Every item the review flags stores
valid markup: Q12 holds p<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub><sup>γ</sup> and
<sup>5/3</sup>, Q24 holds 10<sup>10</sup>-style powers, Q29 and Q31 hold
their exponents and indices as markup, and Q13/Q22 hold real tables. The
export’s flattened forms were extraction artifacts, so nothing was
"corrected". Q34, Q35 and Q37 are the three records that store literal
Unicode superscripts; their anchors use escapes so the stored characters
are unambiguous. "Unanswered", "Report an issue" and "Back to Dashboard"
appear in no stored field anywhere in the physics bank, so they are
interface text and their absence from the signatures is not a stem repair.
New text uses <sup>/<sub> markup with the U+2212 minus this block prefers
inside an exponent, and literal Greek characters, which render identically
to the named entities the older passages use.

deviations: Q1 is a content-exact repeat of the record approved as batch 4 Q34 (phys-214). It is frozen, so it alone keeps the batch 4 list form for its three bodies while Q2-Q41 use lettered paragraphs. The review requires exactly that, so the block ends mixed by design and Q1 adds no coverage.

Where a complete main block is replaced, the stored exp-diagram or centred formula container goes with it, because the review's instruction to keep the existing main/formula layout applies only "unless that main block is explicitly replaced". Q4 and Q5 therefore lose a paragraph on balance; no table was lost, and Q13 and Q22 received their replacement tables.

Three stored feedback headings in Q2-Q11 abbreviated their option text (Q6 D, Q8 A, Q8 D). They were synchronized to the full option text, as the review's heading rule directs. Because some option texts store named entities such as μs and Ω, those entities now also appear in the matching headings; no entity was introduced into prose.
notes: The review's own inventory was cross-checked and closes: 25 stems, four option texts, 11 complete main blocks, seven scoped main passages, 17 Key Concepts, two whole three-point blocks, 11 individual points, five Bottom Lines and 16 replacement distractor bodies, with Q1 the only item carrying no listed edit.

Feedback went from 33 bodies to 123. Q12-Q41 stored none at all, so the 90 supplied bodies were added rather than reconciled; 16 existing bodies were replaced and 17 retained, including Q1's three. None was duplicated.
No answer letter, id, topic or subject moved. Q4 B, Q5 B and Q37 C renamed a keyed option, so those three keyed headings were re-synchronized; Q11 C is a distractor and moved no key.

Q37 is the major numerical repair: the stored calculation mixed the neutral helium-4 ATOMIC mass (4.0026 u) with free-nucleon masses. Consistent nuclear masses, 4.0015 u and 4.0319 u, give 0.0304 u and 28.3 MeV rather than 27.4 MeV. The key stays C, reworded to describe energy released on formation.

Q4, Q5, Q11, Q13, Q22, Q36, Q38 and Q40 are the substantial repairs: Bernoulli's terms and conditions, neutron magnetic moments, property-specific isotropy with a replaced overlapping distractor, positive work versus free expansion, the photoelectric intensity model and its table, the motional-emf geometry, the iron-nickel binding-energy comparison, and slowing fast neutrons rather than a single best shield.

'Unanswered', 'Report an issue' and 'Back to Dashboard' appear in no stored field anywhere in the physics bank, so they are interface text and their absence from the signatures was not treated as a stem repair.

Every item the review flagged for notation already stored valid markup, so nothing was "corrected". No CSS was changed, the approved option-text wrappers and scoped sup/sub rule are untouched, and no bank-wide Unicode conversion was applied.
Structural and consistency checks establish scope and presentation. They do not establish scientific accuracy, which rests on the content review itself.
